title: /create-worktree
summary: The user asks for a new worktree, optionally naming it. The agent inspects the repository, derives a slug, branch and sibling destination, creates the worktree with one git command, verifies it, adopts it as the working directory for every later tool call, and reports the path and branch.
next_flow: Implementation completion: once the task's code is done in this worktree, commit, push and open a pull request against the repository's default branch (SKILL.md lines 21-28).

nodes.name: /create-worktree [name]
nodes.description: The user asks for a new isolated worktree, optionally naming it.

nodes.name: Create worktree
nodes.description: Creates the worktree immediately, without routine follow-up questions, and moves all later work into it.

nodes.name: 1. Identify the repository
nodes.description: Finds the repository root, the current HEAD and the existing worktrees, and remembers the original directory for a later return.

nodes.name: git rev-parse / git worktree list
nodes.description: Asks git where the checkout is and which worktrees already exist.

nodes.name: git rev-parse --show-toplevel; git worktree list
nodes.description: Prints the source root, HEAD and every existing worktree so the slug step can avoid collisions.

nodes.name: Read repository instructions
nodes.description: Reads the AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md that applies at the source root.

nodes.name: 2. Derive slug, branch and destination
nodes.description: Turns the name into a directory slug, derives the codex/<slug> branch and a sibling worktrees directory, and resolves the destination to an absolute path.

nodes.name: name supplied?
nodes.description: The invocation carried a name, or it did not.

nodes.name: Normalize the supplied name
nodes.description: Replaces spaces and unsafe path characters with hyphens and never treats the name as a path or shell code.

nodes.name: Generate a random slug
nodes.description: Makes a short random slug when no name was given.

nodes.name: git check-ref-format --branch
nodes.description: Asks git whether the derived branch name is acceptable.

nodes.name: git check-ref-format --branch
nodes.description: Fails when git would refuse the branch name.

nodes.name: branch or destination exists?
nodes.description: Either the branch or the destination directory is already taken.

nodes.name: Append a random suffix
nodes.description: Appends a short random suffix instead of overwriting or reusing an existing worktree.

nodes.name: 3. Create the worktree
nodes.description: Runs worktree add from the source root with each argument quoted for the active shell and checks the exit status before continuing.

nodes.name: git worktree add -b
nodes.description: Creates the branch and the worktree in one command.

nodes.name: git worktree add
nodes.description: Branches from the committed HEAD into the sibling directory and leaves uncommitted source files where they are.

nodes.name: source checkout dirty?
nodes.description: Uncommitted or untracked files exist in the source checkout.

nodes.name: Mention the dirty source
nodes.description: Says once that uncommitted changes stayed behind in the source checkout.

nodes.name: 4. Verify and adopt the destination
nodes.description: Confirms the new checkout with git, reads its instructions, and makes the absolute destination the explicit workdir for every later tool call.

nodes.name: git -C <destination> rev-parse / branch --show-current
nodes.description: Checks that the destination is a real checkout on the new branch.

nodes.name: git rev-parse --show-toplevel; git branch --show-current
nodes.description: Prints the toplevel and the current branch of the new worktree.

nodes.name: Read the worktree's instructions
nodes.description: Reads the AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md that applies inside the new worktree.

nodes.name: workdir = <absolute destination>
nodes.description: Every subsequent shell call, edit, search and git operation is rooted here, because a shell cd would not persist across tool calls.

nodes.name: 5. Report
nodes.description: Reports the path, the branch, and that subsequent commands run in the worktree.

nodes.name: Path / Branch / I'll run subsequent commands in this worktree.
nodes.description: Three lines the user reads.
